archetype.name: Playoff Team (three-point volume)
archetype.definition: A team whose margin backs up its record, built on the league's most three-heavy, most efficient shot diet and a defense that keeps opponents off the rim, though not yet proven deep enough to be a contender.

report.headline: Portland's 9-3 is earned, but the three-point defense is running hot
report.take:
Portland has arrived ahead of schedule. A franchise that was 42-40 with a -0.3 Net Rtg last season, and a bottom-ten team for most of the years before that, is 9-3, ranks 5th on the site and has a 7.8 Net Rtg, 7th in the league. Nothing about the record is borrowed. W vs Pt Diff sits at 0, and the margin implies exactly the 9 wins they have. This is a real point differential, not a run of coin flips.

The engine is the shot diet. Portland takes 51.5% of its shots from three, first in the league and well above the 43.3 league mark, and it is first or second in eFG %, TS % and FT Rate. That combination of threes and free throws, with very few mid-range shots in between, produces a 120.4 ORtg, 4th in the league. The trend didn't come out of nowhere: the 3PA Rate has climbed each of the last three seasons, from 41.8 to 46.9 to 51.5. The scoring is spread out. Deni Avdija is the hub (3rd of 96 on the SF tab, 5.8 BPM, 29 USG %), and Damian Lillard, Jrue Holiday and Toumani Camara all score efficiently around him. Camara's 68.7 TS % and Holiday's 66.3 are elite for role players.

The numbers hide a few things. The defense is 11th by DRtg, and the 1st-ranked Opp 3P % (32.3, nearly three points under the league) is doing a lot of that work. Some of it is real, because opponents rarely reach the rim (Opp Rim Rate 24.8, 4th), but a three-point percentage this low over 12 games is mostly variance and will drift up. Opposing centers are also feasting: 27.33 points a game, the most in the league and 5.66 over their own averages. The roster is less complete than the record suggests. The backcourt grades only C- because Scoot Henderson has played 265 minutes with a 44.7 TS %, -8.9 BPM and a -15 On-Off while Ja Morant (11.4 On-Off in 4 games) is out. Ball security is a weakness at both ends (TOV % 21st, Opp TOV % 23rd).

The recent form has cooled slightly. The last five games went 3-2 with a +3 margin per game, and November's defense allowed more than October's. Two blowout home losses to Memphis and San Antonio sit next to two convincing wins over Oklahoma City. Expect a good team rather than the 62-win pace: a top-ten offense that stays real, a defense that settles back toward average as the three-point luck fades, and a ceiling that rises when Morant's minutes replace Henderson's.

strengths.title: Threes and free throws, nothing between
strengths.body: Portland leads the league in 3PA Rate and ranks 2nd in FT Rate, which is why its eFG % and TS % both rank 2nd. The approach has deepened over three seasons rather than appearing overnight. Even at 36.5% from three, only 10th, the volume and the free throws carry the efficiency, so it should hold up better than a hot-shooting offense would.

strengths.title: Avdija runs a balanced attack
strengths.body: Avdija is the 3rd-ranked small forward on the site, with a 5.8 BPM and a team-high 1.6 Win Shares on a 29 USG % load. Around him, Lillard (60.9 TS %, +7.2 On-Off), Holiday and Camara score efficiently without needing the ball. No single hot shooter is carrying the offense, which makes it sturdier.

strengths.title: Clingan-Williams frontcourt anchors
strengths.body: The A- frontcourt is the best-graded group. Donovan Clingan ranks 7th among centers, and Robert Williams posts a 5.3 BPM and +11.5 On-Off in his minutes. Together they keep opponents away from the rim (Opp Rim Rate 4th) and give Portland a rebounding edge (REB % 7th).

concerns.title: Defense leaning on opponent misses
concerns.body: Opponents are shooting 32.3% from three against Portland, the lowest in the league and well under the league mark. Over 12 games that is mostly variance. The underlying defense is closer to its 11th-ranked DRtg than to elite, and the November slippage hints the correction has started.

concerns.title: Henderson's minutes with Morant out
concerns.body: Henderson has absorbed real playing time at a 44.7 TS %, -8.9 BPM and a -15 On-Off, and he ranks 85th of 86 at his position. He is the main reason the backcourt grades C-. Morant's +11.4 On-Off in four games shows what the rotation looks like without that hole, so his return is the cleanest upgrade available.

concerns.title: Opposing centers run free
concerns.body: Centers score 27.33 points a game against Portland, the most in the league, and take 24.4% of opponents' points against a league norm of 17%. That is the flip side of a scheme that walls off the rim and runs shooters off the line: bigs get their touches elsewhere. Strong frontcourts will test it.

trend.note: A 4-1 October gave way to a 5-2 November with a leakier defense, and the last five games ran a margin of +3 per game, below the season. Two wins over Oklahoma City keep this reading as a mild cooling rather than a slide.

weekAhead.headline: Five road games, starting with a Minnesota back-to-back
weekAhead.body:
The week is all road games. It opens with consecutive nights in Minnesota against a 9-4 team that ranks 4th on the site and has the league's best defense (105.5 DRtg). The Wolves allow the fewest threes to make an impact: Opp 3P % is 2nd, and small forwards produce less against them relative to their own averages than against anyone. That is a direct hit on Avdija and on a three-heavy offense. The opening lane is the rim, which Minnesota concedes often (Opp Rim Rate 27th) and Portland rarely attacks. Minnesota's offensive rebounding (ORB % 3rd) will also test a Portland glass that is only 11th in DRB %.

Milwaukee in the middle is the breather: 1-13, 28th in DRtg, and soft on centers. The trip closes with two teams better on defense than on offense. New York plays slowly, ranks 4th in DRtg and has an A+ frontcourt that can exploit Portland's leak against centers. Philadelphia is 11-3, but its 2.1 Net Rtg and league-best +3 W vs Pt Diff say it is far less dangerous than its record. Its rim defense is poor (Opp Rim % 22nd, Opp Rim Rate 29th), so Portland's centers should eat. Splitting the two Minnesota games would make this a good week.

keyMatchups.title: Avdija vs Minnesota's wing defense
keyMatchups.body: Minnesota holds small forwards far below their own averages, ranking 1st in that measure for points and threes. Avdija drives Portland's offense, so the Wolves' best defenders will be on its most important player twice in two nights. If he's contained, Lillard and Holiday must carry more of the creation.

keyMatchups.title: Knicks bigs vs Portland's center leak
keyMatchups.body: New York's frontcourt grades A+ and the Knicks rank 2nd in REB %. That is exactly the pressure point for a defense that gives centers the most points in the league. Clingan and Williams must hold the glass in a slow, physical game.

keyMatchups.title: Portland centers at Philly's rim
keyMatchups.body: The 76ers let opponents to the rim more than almost anyone and allow a high finishing rate there. Portland's bigs, Clingan at 63.6 TS % and Williams at 69.6, should find easy points. That makes the trip's finale winnable despite Philadelphia's record.

weekAhead.watch: Whether Portland's three-point volume survives two straight nights against Minnesota's 2nd-ranked three-point defense, the first real test of whether the offense is matchup-proof.

restOfSeason.body:
The offense is the sustainable part. The volume-and-free-throw shot profile has been building for three years, and the shooting itself (36.5% from three, 10th) is not running hot, so a top-five-to-eight offensive rating should hold. The defense will give some back. Opponents won't keep shooting 32.3% from three, and the center vulnerability is structural, so a DRtg nearer league average is the likelier landing spot. The turnover margin, poor on both ends, caps the ceiling.

The 62-win pace overstates it. A Net Rtg settling in the +3 to +5 range points to roughly 49 to 54 wins, comfortably a playoff team in a crowded Northwest. The upside case runs through Morant's return. Replacing Henderson's minutes with a healthy Morant would lift a C- backcourt, and that is the swing that could move Portland from good to genuinely dangerous.
swingFactors: Morant's return and Henderson's minutes shrinking
Opponent 3P % regressing toward the league average
Avdija's health and load at 29 USG %

confidence.note: Margin and record agree, but 12 games and an Opp 3P % that rarely holds.
